verses.zh: 非利士人招聚他们的军旅，要来争战；聚集在属犹大的梭哥，安营在梭哥和亚西加中间的以弗・大悯。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Philistines gathered their troops[NOTE:2] for battle. They assembled at Socoh in Judah. They camped in Ephes Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
notes: The content of 1 Sam 17-18, which includes the David and Goliath story, differs considerably in the LXX as compared to the MT, suggesting that this story circulated in ancient times in more than one form. The LXX for chs. 17-18 is much shorter than the MT, lacking almost half of the material (39 of a total of 88 verses). Many scholars (e.g., McCarter, Klein) think that the shorter text of the LXX is preferable to the MT, which in their view has been expanded by incorporation of later material. Other scholars (e.g., Wellhausen, Driver) conclude that the shorter Greek text (or the Hebrew text that underlies it) reflects an attempt to harmonize certain alleged inconsistencies that appear in the longer version of the story. Given the translation characteristics of the LXX elsewhere in this section, it does not seem likely that these differences are due to deliberate omission of these verses on the part of the translator. It seems more likely that the Greek translator has faithfully rendered here a Hebrew text that itself was much shorter than the MT in these chapters. Whether or not the shorter text represented by the LXX is to be preferred over the MT in 1 Sam 17-18 is a matter over which textual scholars are divided. For a helpful discussion of the major textual issues in this unit see D. Barthélemy, D. W. Gooding, J. Lust, and E. Tov, The Story of David and Goliath (OBO). Overall it seems preferable to stay with the MT, at least for the most part. However, the major textual differences between the LXX and the MT will be mentioned in the notes that accompany the translation so that the reader may be alert to the major problem passages.
Heb “camps.”

verses.zh: 扫罗和以色列人也聚集，在以拉谷安营，摆列队伍，要与非利士人打仗。
verses.en: Saul and the Israelite army[NOTE:1] assembled and camped in the valley of Elah, where they arranged their battle lines to fight against[NOTE:2] the Philistines.
notes: Heb “the men of Israel” (so KJV, NASB); NAB, NIV, NRSV “the Israelites.”
Heb “to meet.”

verses.zh: 非利士人站在这边山上，以色列人站在那边山上，当中有谷。
verses.en: The Philistines were standing on one hill, and the Israelites[NOTE:1] on another hill, with the valley between them.
notes: Heb “Israel.”

verses.zh: 从非利士营中出来一个讨战的人，名叫歌利亚，是迦特人，身高六肘零一虎口；
verses.en: Then a champion[NOTE:1] came out from the camp of the Philistines. His name was Goliath; he was from Gath. He was close to seven feet tall.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the man of the space between the two [armies].” See v. 23.

Heb “his height was six cubits and a span.” The LXX, a Qumran manuscript of 1 Samuel, and Josephus read “four cubits and a span.” A cubit was approximately 17.5 inches, a span half that. So the Masoretic text places Goliath at about 9½ feet tall (cf. NIV84, CEV, NLT “over nine feet”; NCV “nine feet, four inches”; TEV “nearly 3 metres” while the other textual witnesses place him at about 6 feet, 7 inches (cf. NAB “six and a half feet”). Note, too, that the cubit was adjusted through history, also attested in Babylon (NIDOTTE 421-424 s.v. אַמָּה). If the cubits measuring Goliath were reckoned as the cubit of Moses, his height at 6 cubits and a span would be approximately 7 feet 9 inches tall. This is one of many places in Samuel where the LXX and Qumran evidence seems superior to the Masoretic text. It is possible that the scribe’s eye skipped briefly to the number 6 a few lines below in a similar environment of letters. The average Israelite male of the time was about 5 feet 3 inches, so a man 6 feet 7 inches would be a very impressive height. Saul, being head and shoulder above most Israelites, would have been nearly 6 feet tall. That is still shorter than Goliath, even at “four cubits and a span,” and makes a sharper contrast between David and Saul. There would have been a greater expectation that a 6 foot tall Saul would confront a 6 feet 7 inches Goliath, placing Saul in a bad light while still positioning David as a hero of faith, which is fitting to the context.

verses.zh: 头戴铜盔，身穿铠甲，甲重五千舍客勒；
verses.en: He had a bronze helmet on his head and was wearing scale body armor. The weight of his bronze body armor was 5,000 shekels.[NOTE:1]
notes: Although the exact weight of Goliath’s defensive body armor is difficult to estimate in terms of modern equivalency, it was obviously quite heavy. Driver, following Kennedy, suggests a modern equivalent of about 220 pounds (100 kg); see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 139. Klein, taking the shekel to be equal to .403 ounces, arrives at a somewhat smaller weight of about 126 pounds (57 kg); see R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 175. But by any estimate it is clear that Goliath presented himself as a formidable foe indeed.

verses.zh: 腿上有铜护膝，两肩之中背负铜戟；
verses.en: He had bronze shin guards[NOTE:1] on his legs, and a bronze javelin was slung over his shoulders.
notes: Or “greaves.” These were coverings (probably lined for comfort) that extended from about the knee to the ankle, affording protection for the shins of a warrior.

verses.zh: 枪杆粗如织布的机轴，铁枪头重六百舍客勒。有一个拿盾牌的人在他前面走。
verses.en: The shaft[NOTE:1] of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the iron point of his spear weighed 600 shekels.[NOTE:2] His shield bearer was walking before him.
notes: The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading “wood,” rather than the “arrow” (the reading of the Kethib).
That is, about fifteen or sixteen pounds.

verses.zh: 歌利亚对着以色列的军队站立，呼叫说：「你们出来摆列队伍做甚么呢？我不是非利士人吗？你们不是扫罗的仆人吗？可以从你们中间拣选一人，使他下到我这里来。
verses.en: Goliath[NOTE:1] stood and called to Israel’s troops,[NOTE:2] “Why do you come out to prepare for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and are you not the servants of Saul? Choose[NOTE:3] for yourselves a man so he may come down[NOTE:4] to me!
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew text adds “and said to them.”

The translation follows the ancient versions in reading “choose,” (from the root בָּחַר, bakhar), rather than the MT. The verb in MT (בָּרָה, barah) elsewhere means “to eat food”; the sense of “to choose,” required here by the context, is not attested for this root. The MT apparently reflects an early scribal error.
Following the imperative, the prefixed verbal form (either an imperfect or jussive) with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose/result here.

verses.zh: 他若能与我战斗，将我杀死，我们就作你们的仆人；我若胜了他，将他杀死，你们就作我们的仆人，服事我们。」
verses.en: If he is able to fight with me and strike me down, we will become your servants. But if I prevail against him and strike him down, you will become our servants and will serve us.”

verses.zh: 那非利士人又说：「我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我战斗。」
verses.en: Then the Philistine said, “I defy Israel’s troops this day! Give me a man so we can fight[NOTE:1] each other!”
notes: Following the imperative, the cohortative verbal form indicates purpose/result here.

verses.zh: 扫罗和以色列众人听见非利士人的这些话，就惊惶，极其害怕。
verses.en: When Saul and all the Israelites[NOTE:1] heard these words of the Philistine, they were upset and very afraid.
notes: Heb “all Israel.”

verses.zh: 大卫是犹大、伯利恒的以法他人耶西的儿子。耶西有八个儿子。当扫罗的时候，耶西已经老迈。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Now David was the son of an Ephrathite named Jesse from Bethlehem[NOTE:2] in Judah. He had eight sons, and in Saul’s days he was old and well advanced in years.[NOTE:3]
notes: Some mss of the LXX lack vv. 12-31.
For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
The translation follows the Lucianic recension of the LXX and the Syriac Peshitta in reading “in years,” rather than MT “among men.”

verses.zh: 耶西的三个大儿子跟随扫罗出征。这出征的三个儿子：长子名叫以利押，次子名叫亚比拿达，三子名叫沙玛。
verses.en: Jesse’s three oldest sons had followed Saul to war. The names of the[NOTE:1] three sons who went to war were Eliab, his firstborn; Abinadab, the second oldest; and Shammah, the third oldest.
notes: Heb “his.”

verses.zh: 大卫是最小的；那三个大儿子跟随扫罗。
verses.en: Now David was the youngest. While the three oldest sons followed Saul,

verses.zh: 大卫有时离开扫罗，回伯利恒放他父亲的羊。
verses.en: David was going back and forth[NOTE:1] from Saul in order to care for his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.
notes: Heb “was going and returning.”

verses.zh: 那非利士人早晚都出来站着，如此四十日。
verses.en: Meanwhile for 40 days the Philistine approached every morning and evening and took his position.

verses.zh: 一日，耶西对他儿子大卫说：「你拿一伊法烘了的穗子和十个饼，速速地送到营里去，交给你哥哥们；
verses.en: Jesse said to his son David, “Take your brothers this ephah of roasted grain and these 10 loaves of bread; go quickly[NOTE:1] to the camp to your brothers.
notes: Heb “run.”

verses.zh: 再拿这十块奶饼，送给他们的千夫长，且问你哥哥们好，向他们要一封信来。」
verses.en: Also take these 10 portions of cheese to their commanding officer.[NOTE:1] Find out how your brothers are doing[NOTE:2] and bring back their pledge that they received the goods.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “officer of the thousand.”
Heb “and your brothers, observe with respect to welfare.”

Heb “and their pledge take.” This probably refers to some type of confirmation that the goods arrived safely. See R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 177. Cf. NIV “bring back some assurance”; NCV “some proof to show me they are all right”; NLT “bring me back a letter from them.”

verses.zh: 扫罗与大卫的三个哥哥和以色列众人，在以拉谷与非利士人打仗。
verses.en: They are with Saul and the whole Israelite army[NOTE:1] in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.”
notes: Heb “all the men of Israel.”

verses.zh: 大卫早晨起来，将羊交托一个看守的人，照着他父亲所吩咐的话，带着食物去了。到了辎重营，军兵刚出到战场，呐喊要战。
verses.en: So David got up early in the morning and entrusted the flock to someone else who would watch over it.[NOTE:1] After loading up, he went just as Jesse had instructed him. He arrived at the camp[NOTE:2] as the army was going out to the battle lines shouting its battle cry.
notes: Heb “to a guard”; KJV, NASB, NRSV “with a keeper”; NIV11 “in the care of a shepherd.” Since in contemporary English “guard” sounds like someone at a military installation or a prison, the present translation uses “to someone else who would watch over it.”
Or “entrenchment.”

verses.zh: 以色列人和非利士人都摆列队伍，彼此相对。
verses.en: Israel and the Philistines drew up their battle lines opposite one another.

verses.zh: 大卫把他带来的食物留在看守物件人的手下，跑到战场，问他哥哥们安。
verses.en: After David had entrusted his cargo to the care of the supply officer,[NOTE:1] he ran to the battlefront. When he arrived, he asked his brothers how they were doing.
notes: Heb “the guard of the equipment.”

verses.zh: 与他们说话的时候，那讨战的，就是属迦特的非利士人歌利亚，从非利士队中出来，说从前所说的话；大卫都听见了。
verses.en: As he was speaking with them, the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, was coming up from the battle lines of the Philistines. He spoke the way he usually did,[NOTE:1] and David heard it.
notes: Heb “according to these words.”

verses.zh: 以色列众人看见那人，就逃跑，极其害怕。
verses.en: When all the men of Israel saw this man, they retreated[NOTE:1] from his presence and were very afraid.
notes: Or “fled.”

verses.zh: 以色列人彼此说：「这上来的人你看见了吗？他上来是要向以色列人骂阵。若有能杀他的，王必赏赐他大财，将自己的女儿给他为妻，并在以色列人中免他父家纳粮当差。」
verses.en: The men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who is coming up? He does so[NOTE:1] to defy Israel. But the king will make the man who can strike him down very wealthy! He will give him his daughter in marriage, and he will make his father’s house exempt from tax obligations in Israel.”
notes: Heb “he is coming up.”

verses.zh: 大卫问站在旁边的人说：「有人杀这非利士人，除掉以色列人的耻辱，怎样待他呢？这未受割礼的非利士人是谁呢？竟敢向永生　神的军队骂阵吗？」
verses.en: David asked the men who were standing near him, “What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and frees Israel from this humiliation?[NOTE:1] For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he defies the armies of the living God?”
notes: Heb “and turns aside humiliation from upon Israel.”

verses.zh: 百姓照先前的话回答他说：「有人能杀这非利士人，必如此如此待他。」
verses.en: The soldiers[NOTE:1] told him what had been promised, saying,[NOTE:2] “This is what will be done for the man who can strike him down.”
notes: Heb “people.”
Heb “according to this word, saying.”

verses.zh: 大卫的长兄以利押听见大卫与他们所说的话，就向他发怒，说：「你下来做甚么呢？在旷野的那几只羊，你交托了谁呢？我知道你的骄傲和你心里的恶意，你下来特为要看争战！」
verses.en: When David’s[NOTE:1] oldest brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men, he became angry[NOTE:2] with David and said, “Why have you come down here? To whom did you entrust those few sheep in the wilderness? I am familiar with your pride and deceit![NOTE:3] You have come down here to watch the battle.”
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the anger of Eliab became hot.”
Heb “the wickedness of your heart.”

verses.zh: 大卫说：「我做了甚么呢？我来岂没有缘故吗？」
verses.en: David replied, “What have I done now? Can’t I say anything?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Is it not [just] a word?”

verses.zh: 大卫就离开他转向别人，照先前的话而问；百姓仍照先前的话回答他。
verses.en: Then he turned from those who were nearby to someone else and asked the same question,[NOTE:1] but they[NOTE:2] gave him the same answer as before.
notes: Heb “and spoke according to this word.”
Heb “the people.”

verses.zh: 有人听见大卫所说的话，就告诉了扫罗；扫罗便打发人叫他来。
verses.en: When David’s words were overheard and reported to Saul, he called for him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he took him.”

verses.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「人都不必因那非利士人胆怯。你的仆人要去与那非利士人战斗。」
verses.en: David said to Saul, “Don’t let anyone be discouraged.[NOTE:1] Your servant will go and fight this Philistine!”
notes: Heb “Let not the heart of a man fall upon him.” The LXX reads “my lord,” instead of “a man.”

verses.zh: 扫罗对大卫说：「你不能去与那非利士人战斗；因为你年纪太轻，他自幼就作战士。」
verses.en: But Saul replied to David, “You aren’t able to go against this Philistine and fight him. You’re just a boy! He has been a warrior from his youth.”

verses.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「你仆人为父亲放羊，有时来了狮子，有时来了熊，从群中衔一只羊羔去。
verses.en: David replied to Saul, “Your servant has been a shepherd for his father’s flock. Whenever a lion or bear would come and carry off a sheep from the flock,

verses.zh: 我就追赶它，击打它，将羊羔从它口中救出来。它起来要害我，我就揪着它的胡子，将它打死。
verses.en: I would go out after it, strike it down, and rescue the sheep from its mouth. If it rose up against me, I would grab it by its jaw, strike it, and kill it.

verses.zh: 你仆人曾打死狮子和熊，这未受割礼的非利士人向永生　神的军队骂阵，也必像狮子和熊一般。」
verses.en: Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine will be just like one of them,[NOTE:1] for he has defied the armies of the living God.”
notes: The LXX includes here the following words not found in the MT: “Should I not go and smite him, and remove today reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised one?”

verses.zh: 大卫又说：「耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。」扫罗对大卫说：「你可以去吧！耶和华必与你同在。」
verses.en: David went on to say, “The Lord who delivered me from the lion and the bear will also deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” Then Saul said to David, “Go! The Lord will be with you.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “Go, and may the Lord be with you” (so NASB, NCV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 扫罗就把自己的战衣给大卫穿上，将铜盔给他戴上，又给他穿上铠甲。
verses.en: Then Saul clothed David with his own fighting attire and put a bronze helmet on his head. He also put body armor on him.

verses.zh: 大卫把刀跨在战衣外，试试能走不能走；因为素来没有穿惯，就对扫罗说：「我穿戴这些不能走，因为素来没有穿惯。」于是摘脱了。
verses.en: David strapped on his sword over his fighting attire and tried to walk around, but he was not used to them.[NOTE:1] David said to Saul, “I can’t walk in these things, for I’m not used to them.” So David removed them.
notes: Heb “he had not tested.”

verses.zh: 他手中拿杖，又在溪中挑选了五块光滑石子，放在袋里，就是牧人带的囊里；手中拿着甩石的机弦，就去迎那非利士人。
verses.en: He took his staff in his hand, picked out five smooth stones from the stream, placed them in the pouch[NOTE:1] of his shepherd’s bag, took his sling in hand, and approached the Philistine.
notes: This Hebrew word occurs only here and its exact meaning is not entirely clear. It refers to a receptacle of some sort and apparently was a common part of a shepherd’s equipment. Here it serves as a depository for the stones that David will use in his sling.

verses.zh: 非利士人也渐渐地迎着大卫来，拿盾牌的走在前头。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Philistine, with his shield bearer walking in front of him, kept coming closer to David.
notes: Most LXX mss lack v. 41.

verses.zh: 非利士人观看，见了大卫，就藐视他；因为他年轻，面色光红，容貌俊美。
verses.en: When the Philistine looked carefully at David, he despised him, for he was only a ruddy and handsome boy.

verses.zh: 非利士人对大卫说：「你拿杖到我这里来，我岂是狗呢？」非利士人就指着自己的神咒诅大卫。
verses.en: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you are coming after me with sticks?”[NOTE:1] Then the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
notes: Sticks is a pejorative reference to David’s staff (v. 40); the same Hebrew word (מַקֵּל, maqqel) is used for both.

verses.zh: 非利士人又对大卫说：「来吧！我将你的肉给空中的飞鸟、田野的走兽吃。」
verses.en: The Philistine said to David, “Come here to me, so I can give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the field!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss have “the earth” here, instead of the MT’s “the field.”

verses.zh: 大卫对非利士人说：「你来攻击我，是靠着刀枪和铜戟；我来攻击你，是靠着万军之耶和华的名，就是你所怒骂带领以色列军队的　神。
verses.en: But David replied to the Philistine, “You are coming against me with sword and spear and javelin. But I am coming against you in the name of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel’s armies, whom you have defied!

verses.zh: 今日耶和华必将你交在我手里。我必杀你，斩你的头，又将非利士军兵的尸首给空中的飞鸟、地上的野兽吃，使普天下的人都知道以色列中有　神；
verses.en: This very day the Lord will deliver you into my hand. I will strike you down and cut off your head. This day I will give the corpses of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the land. Then all the land will realize that Israel has a God,

verses.zh: 又使这众人知道耶和华使人得胜，不是用刀用枪，因为争战的胜败全在乎耶和华。他必将你们交在我们手里。」
verses.en: and all this assembly will know that it is not by sword or spear that the Lord saves! For the battle is the Lord’s, and he will deliver you into our hand.”

verses.zh: 非利士人起身，迎着大卫前来。大卫急忙迎着非利士人，往战场跑去。
verses.en: The Philistine drew steadily closer to David to attack him, while David quickly ran toward the battle line to attack the Philistine.[NOTE:1]
notes: Most LXX mss lack the second half of v. 48.

verses.zh: 大卫用手从囊中掏出一块石子来，用机弦甩去，打中非利士人的额，石子进入额内，他就仆倒，面伏于地。
verses.en: David reached his hand into the bag and took out a stone. He slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank deeply into his forehead, and he fell down with his face to the ground.

verses.zh: 这样，大卫用机弦甩石，胜了那非利士人，打死他；大卫手中却没有刀。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] David prevailed over the Philistine with just the sling and the stone. He struck down the Philistine and killed him. David did not even have a sword in his hand.[NOTE:2]
notes: Most LXX mss lack v. 50.
Verse 50 is a summary statement; v. 51 gives a more detailed account of how David killed the Philistine.

verses.zh: 大卫跑去，站在非利士人身旁，将他的刀从鞘中拔出来，杀死他，割了他的头。非利士众人看见他们讨战的勇士死了，就都逃跑。
verses.en: David ran and stood over the Philistine. He grabbed Goliath’s[NOTE:1] sword, drew it from its sheath,[NOTE:2] and after killing him, he cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they ran away.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Most LXX mss lack the words “drew it from its sheath.”

verses.zh: 以色列人和犹大人便起身呐喊，追赶非利士人，直到迦特（或译：该）和以革伦的城门。被杀的非利士人倒在沙拉音的路上，直到迦特和以革伦。
verses.en: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward, shouting a battle cry.[NOTE:1] They chased the Philistines to the valley[NOTE:2] and to the very gates of Ekron. The Philistine corpses lay fallen along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
notes: Heb “arose and cried out.”
Most of the LXX ms tradition has here “Gath.”

verses.zh: 以色列人追赶非利士人回来，就夺了他们的营盘。
verses.en: When the Israelites returned from their hot pursuit of the Philistines, they looted their camp.

verses.zh: 大卫将那非利士人的头拿到耶路撒冷，却将他军装放在自己的帐棚里。
verses.en: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] and he put Goliath’s[NOTE:2] weapons in his tent.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “his”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 扫罗看见大卫去攻击非利士人，就问元帅押尼珥说：「押尼珥啊，那少年人是谁的儿子？」押尼珥说：「我敢在王面前起誓，我不知道。」
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Now as Saul watched David going out to fight the Philistine, he asked Abner, the general in command of the army, “Whose son is that young man, Abner?” Abner replied, “As surely as you live, O king, I don’t know.”
notes: Most LXX mss lack 17:55-18:5.

verses.zh: 王说：「你可以问问那幼年人是谁的儿子。」
verses.en: The king said, “Find out whose son this boy is.”

verses.zh: 大卫打死非利士人回来，押尼珥领他到扫罗面前，他手中拿着非利士人的头。
verses.en: So when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul. He still had the head of the Philistine in his hand.

verses.zh: 扫罗问他说：「少年人哪，你是谁的儿子？」大卫说：「我是你仆人伯利恒人耶西的儿子。」
verses.en: Saul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” David replied, “I am the son of your servant Jesse in Bethlehem.”[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
